"May effective dates span 1-28 May" while the postings cluster at month-end, supporting a posting-time rather than event-time explanation.

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Re-plot the trend pack on effective_event_date instead of posted_at to confirm the spike flattens (read-only, reversible)."
"In parallel, confirm recognition basis with Revenue Assurance and request dealer master to verify the West-region mapping."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "Do NOT reverse or hold the 17 postings: reconciled, unique, and matched to the cent" gives a clear operational decision.
"If spike persists after re-keying or contract cannot be confirmed, escalate the cadence change" provides a specific escalation trigger.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "The cluster is a reconciled West-dealer posting-timing pattern, not duplicate revenue, period-stuffing, or manipulation." The posting-time explanation is well supported, but ruling out manipulation or period-stuffing is stronger than the evidence permits because the contract, dealer mapping, and field semantics remain unverified.

"even under the worst-case reading this is immaterial." Dollar materiality alone does not establish that an erroneous posting or reporting-control issue is immaterial, and the submission does not cite a formal materiality threshold.
"Amounts ~12x monthly per plan ... ruling out inflation." The amount relationship is consistent with annual versus monthly billing, but does not by itself rule out pricing or reporting manipulation.

"Pipeline defect: rejected. All 41 files RECONCILED, rows_accepted = rows_received, posted >= effective always." These checks substantially reduce evidence of a pipeline defect, but do not prove that every possible pipeline or field-semantics defect is absent.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The analyst handled the strongest benign alternative—month-end batching of genuine events—well and also considered duplicate revenue, unauthorized cadence change, recognition timing, and dealer-ID mis-mapping. The main missed or underweighted alternative is that the cadence change could reflect an unauthorized process or reporting manipulation even if row counts and cash reconcile; the submission notes this possibility but its headline conclusion rejects manipulation too categorically.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Soften the causal conclusion from definitive rejection to a calibrated finding: no evidence of duplicate cash or entitlement impact, with the posting-time explanation strongly supported but contingent on confirming the dealer mapping, contract/process authorization, and recognition basis; explicitly test entitlement impact rather than relying mainly on recharge uniqueness and cash reconciliation.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "South CareDesk tickets fell from 175 in January to 104 in June, while control regions were broadly flat: E 101→102, N 168→170, W 176→169."
"NovaIVR generated 2,709 South sessions, with 650 ending at `authenticate`; that is 24.0% of NOVA sessions, and these sessions have no verified customer case in the CareDesk view."

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "My inference is that complaint volume was suppressed by channel filtering: 24.0% of sessions (650/2,709) in `ivr_interactions.jsonl` dropped out at the authentication stage without creating CareDesk tickets."
"While genuine deflection occurred for routine queries (29.1% balance checks, 21.3% pack info), unresolved technical issues went unrecorded."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "Recorded South CareDesk cases fell from 175 to 104, but the supplied data cannot distinguish genuine resolution from changed authentication and case-creation measurement."
"I cannot test whether failed-authentication customers contact SkyWave again without a read-only subscriber-level 7-day callback/recontact query."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Decision: Do not expand NovaIVR nationally yet; keep the South pilot at its current scope while measuring contacts like-for-like."
"It is cheap and fully reversible: it writes no customer record, changes no routing, and its output can be discarded."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "The single next action is one targeted, read-only 7-day repeat-contact/callback query reconciled to all NOVA sessions."
"Which exact terminal stages and outcomes are excluded from the containment denominator?"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "representing genuine deflection for authenticated callers" is stronger than the stage data supports; a balance_check or pack_info terminal stage does not by itself establish successful resolution or improved customer experience.

"unresolved technical issues went unrecorded" is plausible but not demonstrated solely by authentication-stage termination and missing CareDesk cases; the sessions may have recovered through another channel or may not have represented complaints.

"This divergence refutes the claim that fewer logged tickets prove fewer customer issues" is directionally reasonable, but service-event counts and affected-account estimates are not direct measures of customer friction or complaint volume and may not move one-for-one with cases.

"the interaction log ... shows errors and abandoned sessions that do not become CareDesk cases" needs more explicit linkage between the relevant error/abandonment records and absent downstream cases; the submission does not provide sampled journey or call evidence.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The submission handled genuine routine self-service containment as an alternative to pure measurement failure, but it missed the strongest benign interpretation: authentication-stage abandonment may include non-complaint interactions, and service-event exposure may remain high without producing equivalent complaint demand. Thus the observed divergence supports a capture-failure hypothesis but does not by itself establish that customers experienced unresolved harm.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Add end-to-end validation rather than relying primarily on the repeat-contact query: link a sample of NOVA sessions to subsequent contacts and outcomes, and listen to sampled authentication failures/abandonments. This would test whether the missing cases are unresolved complaints, successful recovery, or non-complaint abandonment.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission cites inverter_events.csv rows 1-4 and specific fields: event, severity, duration_min, inverter_id, impact_mw, and cleared.
It explicitly distinguishes observed values from unknowns, stating that zero impact may not distinguish affected from healthy units and that export completeness is unknown.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: It triangulates severity, duration, inverter identity, impact_mw, and cleared status to reject an ongoing generation-impacting fault.
It rejects the equipment-failure hypothesis for stated reasons, but the analysis remains within one CSV rather than independently verifying through plant or operational channels.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The conclusion is explicitly limited to 'the four provided rows' and does not claim the export is complete.
It identifies the smallest useful uncertainty-reducing check: a read-only, unfiltered event query, while acknowledging that whether zero is measured or defaulted is unknown.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: 'Do not escalate on these records; request one cheap completeness check before broader analysis' is proportionate to zero recorded impact, cleared status, short durations, and lack of recurrence.
'Make no equipment or configuration changes' preserves operational safety, and the proposed query can distinguish an incomplete export from a complete low-severity set.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion accurately stops at an extract-level assessment and says to reassess only if additional open, recurring, or nonzero-impact events emerge.
It does not invent a plant problem from the warning event and correctly treats the completeness question as unresolved rather than as evidence of escalation.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: 'No escalation signal' is appropriately qualified to the supplied extract, but could be read too broadly if the scope limitation is overlooked.

The claim that the records provide 'no basis for equipment intervention' is defensible for the supplied rows, but cannot exclude an unrelated plant-wide issue outside the export. No material unsupported claim is otherwise evident.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The constant impact_mw = 0 and cleared = yes values could be defaulted, incompletely populated, or drawn from an incomplete export; therefore the records may understate plant conditions even though they do not themselves demonstrate a fault.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Add a low-priority quality check for the mixed event wording and, if available, verify one event against an independent operational source such as SCADA impact or inverter telemetry; otherwise retain the justified stop after the completeness query.

dimensions.name: A. Evidence traceability
citations: The submission cites specific fields and files for the same-day calculation: "dispatch_blocks.csv, base_schedule_mw, submitted_schedule_mw, actual_mw, dsm_rate_rs_kwh, schedule_source."
It explicitly distinguishes arithmetic confidence from causal confidence: "High for arithmetic; Medium for causal interpretation."
It reproduces the headline calculation using the dated daily sums and identifies the different-day comparison.

dimensions.name: B. Investigative reasoning
citations: The submission tests the central alternative by comparing 28 May with the 29 May same-day base-versus-submitted counterfactual.
It triangulates penalty totals, absolute deviation metrics, firmware and wind fields, daily variability, and commercial settlement limitations.
It examines innocent explanations and causal threats: "Forecast skill vs hindsight" and "Net commercial value."

dimensions.name: C. Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The submission states that neither estimate establishes a general causal effect and labels the 17.6% result as "descriptive/model-based evidence for that day, not causal proof."
It identifies concrete decision-changing evidence: immutable pre-submission timestamps and a complete net commercial settlement calculation.
It avoids both overclaiming the 31.6% result and the opposite error of dismissing the pilot entirely.

dimensions.name: D. Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation to keep scope unchanged and use a "read-only shadow calculation" is reversible and does not alter submitted schedules or plant control.
The next test is discriminating: several matched high-wind days, immutable timestamps, base-versus-submitted shadow calculations, and net commercial value.
The recommendation preserves the legitimate operational value of continued piloting while placing expansion on hold.

dimensions.name: E. Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion directly satisfies the key distinction: "Insufficient evidence that the AI pilot caused a 31.6% improvement."
It retains the smaller same-day benefit: "the stronger same-day modeled estimate is about 17.6%."
It accurately scopes 31.6% as a descriptive two-day difference rather than a controlled causal estimate.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The statement that verified pre-submission timestamps would "validate predictive skill" is too strong: timestamps establish that adjustments preceded realization, but do not by themselves demonstrate forecast skill or causal benefit.

The statement that post-hoc adjustments would "invalidate the AI claim" is overbroad; they would undermine a claim of prospective predictive efficacy, but might not invalidate every possible operational or descriptive claim.

The proposed same-day 17.6% estimate is appropriately qualified, but its validity still depends on the documented banded penalty model being an appropriate counterfactual and on base and submitted schedules being comparable in all relevant respects.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The pilot may have produced a genuine positive operational effect on 29 May, and the 17.6% same-day modeled reduction is directionally supportive. However, event-specific conditions, schedule selection, model assumptions, and the absence of prospective timestamps prevent attributing that reduction confidently to AI or generalizing it to the 31.6% cross-day headline.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Obtain immutable pre-submission forecast and schedule timestamps, then run a pre-registered set of matched high-wind shadow evaluations with complete net-settlement accounting. This would most directly distinguish prospective pilot skill from hindsight and determine whether the modeled penalty reduction creates net commercial value.

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Place a reversible mapping hold and request Tares/ruling confirmation."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Swiss Matrix ... warns Swiss/EU strings need not match" is asserted without a precise quoted passage or row reference to the warning.
"No record contradicts 90211000" is a broad negative claim; it should be scoped to the reviewed records and the applicable effective-date source.

"This ... [is] the only legal fact still unresolved in evidence" may overlook the separately identified unresolved invoice-value presentation and any need to confirm the exact tariff edition or ruling scope.
The statement that "90211000 closes it" is somewhat categorical unless the Tares/ruling confirmation is verified for the shipment date, jurisdiction, product facts and applicable edition.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: 90211000 may not be the legally applicable Swiss code on 4 November 2025, or the product facts could support a different national classification; alternatively, the CHF 126,900 presentation could affect the customs calculation. These possibilities justify verification, but the cited evidence currently better supports a benign Swiss-versus-Helios code-system mismatch than an established declaration error.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Precisely verify and cite the effective Swiss Tares/ruling record for 4 November 2025, including jurisdiction, tariff edition, product facts and ruling scope, while reconciling the invoice-value presentation before declaring the false positive closed.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "IE-2025-000411 declares P1006 with Preference=Yes, United States origin, 0.0% duty, and 90211090."
"The only Irish-origin register entry supplied for P1006 is SUP-02, valid 2025-01-01 to 2025-07-31 and marked ‘Expired in register’; the shipment date is 2025-09-18."
"The airway bill links SHP-000411 to IE-2025-000411 but provides no `supplier_id`; the packet manifest lists six files and no shipment-specific supplier declaration."
"The reference lookup says no current document was found for SUP-02/P1006 and expressly says absence from the register does not prove that no document exists outside it."

The submission generally ties material facts to named files, rows, dates, and fields, but occasionally treats the register as if it were itself the supplier declaration and relies on "review_note.txt" without otherwise establishing its contents in the evidence table.

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: "Unsupported is not the same as false. Verdict: unsupported, not disproved."
"‘Preference indicator alone validates preferential treatment’: rejected because preferential origin requires an active, linked supplier declaration"
"‘Commercial manufacturing country in commercial_invoice.pdf disproves preference’: rejected because manufacturing origin was never designed to prove preferential origin"
"‘The shipment should be flagged for fraud’: rejected because absence of a supplier declaration ... represents unverified documentation, not intentional misdeclaration."

The submission tests the main competing interpretations and distinguishes manufacturing country from preferential origin, but it does not fully test whether another accepted proof of origin could support preference without the specific supplier declaration it assumes is required.

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: "The preferential origin claim ... is unsupported on current evidence; hold pending documentation."
"Unsupported is not the same as false. Verdict: unsupported, not disproved."
"The register explicitly notes that absence from the table does not prove no document exists outside it."
"My inference is that this represents an evidence-tracking gap rather than commercial misrepresentation."
Confidence is appropriately limited, missing evidence is precisely identified, and the submission avoids declaring fraud or definitively invalidating the claim.

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "The airway bill links SHP-000411 to IE-2025-000411 but provides no `supplier_id`"
"the packet manifest lists six files and no shipment-specific supplier declaration."
"Resolving which supplier fulfilled this shipment and obtaining their valid declaration from ... procurement folders ... is the required proof."
"Distinguishing unverified documentation from intentional misdeclaration ensures that administrative holds precede any formal compliance escalation."

The response identifies the key data-lineage failure—shipment-to-supplier linkage—and explains how procurement records could resolve it. It could better explain the governing origin rule and the distinction between a register entry, a supplier declaration, and other possible origin evidence.

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "The correct disposition is a reversible hold, not an error or fraud referral."
"Place a reversible administrative hold on the preference claim."
"Request the active supplier declaration and originating rule from Procurement."
"Treat the line as non-preferential (0.0% duty neutral) until documentary proof is verified, without initiating an irreversible voluntary disclosure."

The proposed hold and evidence request are proportionate and reversible. However, directing that the claim be treated as non-preferential and then "removing preference claim" should be conditioned on the applicable customs procedure and verified impact, even if the stated duty is 0.0%.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "preferential origin requires an active, linked supplier declaration" is too categorical without identifying the applicable trade agreement and whether other accepted proofs, such as an invoice origin declaration or other prescribed evidence, could establish preference.
"obtaining their valid declaration from `supplier_origin_register.csv`" conflates a register record with the underlying supplier declaration; the register may only be an index or status record.
"Valid declaration flips decision to clear as preferential" is overbroad because validity, coverage, supplier identity, originating rule, and shipment applicability would all still need verification.

"SUP-03/05/06 would allow linking active preference" is unsupported as written: current entries for those suppliers do not by themselves prove that one supplied this shipment or that its declaration covers the shipment.

"absence of a supplier declaration in `review_note.txt` and ClearView" is not fully traceable in the submission because the cited review note and ClearView record are not separately described with specific fields or passages.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The claim may be supportable through an accepted origin declaration or other prescribed supplier evidence held outside the six-file packet; the expired SUP-02 register entry and absent shipment-to-supplier link therefore establish an evidence gap, not necessarily an invalid preference claim. Conversely, if no qualifying evidence can be linked to the actual supplier and applicable rule, the preference should be corrected even though the stated 0.0% duty means no immediate duty difference.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Identify the applicable preferential trade rule and enumerate all accepted forms of proof, then obtain and link the actual supplier and shipment-specific origin evidence before deciding whether to clear or correct the claim.

citations: "'The data is broken and should be discarded': rejected because timestamps ... have no negative durations ... the main problem is semantic fitness for the KPI, not arithmetic corruption."
"'The 45.5-hour average is the SOP cycle time': rejected because `qc_release_sop.md` starts at required-evidence availability"

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "Required evidence availability timestamp | Live QCore timestamp audit capturing true certificate upload times"
"True disposition time of 02:10 batches | Read-only live audit of 10 batches with 02:10:00 extract timestamps"
"obtaining verified upload timestamps would resolve the true start of the release clock before building any report."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The statement that 70.6% of release timestamps are definitively "synthetic snapshot artifacts" is somewhat stronger than the timestamp concentration and freshness evidence alone establish; they could also reflect scheduled or batched interface commits. The submission appropriately proposes a live audit to test this.

The phrase "excluding those completed rows gives an evidence-to-release median of about 8.4 hours" is not fully defined because the extract lacks the required-evidence timestamp; it should be labeled explicitly as a proxy and tied to its actual start field.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 02:10:00 concentration may reflect legitimate scheduled or batched release/interface commits rather than a purely synthetic artifact, and the apparent long cycle time could therefore combine real workflow delay with extract timing. An event log or verified decision-time audit is needed to distinguish these explanations.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Request the event/decision timestamp definition and a small event-log extract for sampled batches, joined to a coherent snapshot, rather than relying primarily on `qcore_release_ts`; this would directly separate true workflow duration from interface or snapshot timing and establish whether any KPI is computable.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: "Every search hit represents a direct transfer opportunity": rejected" using reserved MTR-4401 stock and zero stock at HA-0002.
"Same part family means interchangeable": rejected" using revision A versus revision B and the approval requirement.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "Manufacturer part number and revision from maintenance records" for the 11 blank-part-number requests.
"Live local CMMS reservation and availability query" for negative or stale availability.
"Receiving engineer and qualification approval" for revision substitutions.
"Compare recall/precision of exact MPN join versus semantic search" to determine whether a pilot is justified.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "An exact MPN join resolves all 13 identified requests immediately" overstates what the join establishes: it retrieves identity candidates, but does not resolve current availability, reservation, qualification, revision, or transferability.

"Semantic search is not the real problem" and "Master-data hygiene, not search, is the priority" are too categorical because the 11 blank-MPN requests remain precisely the population where semantic search may add candidate-generation value.
The label "actionable now" is somewhat overstated given the stated 26 June global stock snapshot and the admission that live confirmation is still required.

"All four not-transferable requests" is stronger than the evidence warrants if reservation and zero-stock records may be stale or erroneous; the submission itself says a live CMMS check could revive the hypothesis.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: Exact MPN matching is a strong baseline and safely identifies candidates, but semantic search may still be valuable for the 11 blank-MPN requests and for recovering equivalent descriptions. The right conclusion is likely a constrained semantic-search pilot for candidate generation, with manufacturer identity, revision, UOM, qualification, reservation, and current-availability confirmation before any transfer.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Run a targeted, current-date validation of the 13 exact-MPN candidates and the 11 blank-MPN requests: query live CMMS reservations/availability and obtain manufacturer part number plus revision from maintenance records. Measure semantic-search precision and incremental valid-match recall against that adjudicated set before declaring data cleanup superior to search.
